Section 3 derives the sum-rate as a chain of equations in running text with no proof environment; represented as equation nodes linked by uses edges rather than one proof node.

nodes.name: Two-way relay network
nodes.statement:
To overcome this
drawback, a two-way (or bi-directional) relay network has been
presented in \cite{RW:07:JSAC}, where two nodes, namely $\Source{1}$
and $\Source{2}$, transmit simultaneously to the relay $\mathsf{R}$ in
the first hop, and in the second hop the relay $\mathsf{R}$ forwards its
received signals to both terminals $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$.

nodes.name: Two-way AF distributed Alamouti space-time code (DASTC) protocol
nodes.statement:
The communications of the proposed two-way AF DASTC scheme occur in
three phases. In the first phase, both $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$
transmit the first row of Alamouti code \cite{Ala:98:JSAC} to
$\mathsf{R}$ with the same transmit power per symbol $\mathcal{P}_s$. The received
signal at the relay $\mathsf{R}$ is given by


\begin{align} \y{R} = \h{1} \s{1} + \h{2} \x{1} + \B{n}_{\mathsf{R}}
\end{align}


where $\s{1}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{s_1 } & {s_2 }  \\
\end{array}}]$ and $\x{1}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{x_1 } & {x_2 }  \\
\end{array}}]$ are the two first rows of the Alamouti codes generated
by $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, respectively. The channel
coefficients for the link from $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ to
$\mathsf{R}$, respectively denoted as $\h{1}$ and $\h{2}$, follow a
Rayleigh distribution, i.e., $\h{1} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{1}}$ and $\h{2}
\sim \CG{0}{\CP{2}}$. The vector $\B{n}_{\mathsf{R}}$ is the complex additive white
Gaussian noise (AWGN) with zero mean and variance $N_0$.

In the second phase, $\mathsf{R}$ amplifies the received signal, i.e.,
$\y{R}$, with the same power constraint as in the first phase and
forwards to $\Source{2}$ while $\Source{1}$ sends the second row of
the Alamouti code to $\Source{2}$. The received signal at the source
$\Source{2}$, $\y{2}$, is written as


\begin{align} \y{2}
   =
   \h{2} G \y{R} + \h{0} \s{2} + \n{2}
\end{align}


where $G$ is the scalar amplifying gain at the relay, $\h{0}
\sim \CG{0}{\CP{0}}$ is the channel gain for the link between
$\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, $\s{2}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{-s_2^{\ast} } & {s_1^{\ast} }  \\
\end{array}}]$ is the second row of the Alamouti code, and $\n{2}$ is
the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.

Similarly, in the third phase, $\mathsf{R}$ transmit $G \y{R}$
whereas $\Source{2}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to
$\Source{1}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{1}$,
$\y{1}$, is shown as


\begin{align} \y{1}
   =
   \h{1} G \y{R} + \h{0} \x{2} + \n{1}
\end{align}


where $\x{2}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{-x_2^{\ast} } & {x_1^{\ast} }  \\
\end{array}}]$ is the second row of Alamouti code and $\n{1}$ is
the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.

nodes.name: Average sum-rate
nodes.statement:
As mentioned above, since the
channel model is assumed to be ergodic block fading, we can describe
the average sum-rate as follows:


\begin{align} C_{\text{sum}}
    &=
    \mathbb{E}
    \biggl\{
    \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+G^2 |\h{2}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{s}}\B{h} \right)
    \nonumber
    \\
    &+
    \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+ G^2 |\h{1}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{x}}\B{h} \right)
    \biggr\}
\end{align}


where $\R{\B{s}}$ and $\R{\B{x}}$ are the covariance matrices of
Gaussian codewords and the pre-factor $2/3$ accounts for the fact
that each source received information consisting of two symbols over
three time slots.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.statement_short: Average sum-rate as expected sum of two log-det mutual informations, pre-factor 2/3 for three slots.

nodes.name: Average sum-rate expression
nodes.statement: C_{\text{sum}} &= \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+G^2 |\h{2}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{s}}\B{h} \right) \nonumber \\ &+ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+ G^2 |\h{1}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{x}}\B{h} \right) \biggr\}
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.label: eq:SumRate:1

nodes.name: Codeword covariance of Alamouti codes
nodes.statement:
Due to the orthogonality of Alamouti codeword, it
is easy to see that $\R{\B{s}} = \EX{\B{S} \B{S}^{\dag}} = 2\mathcal{P}_s
\B{I}_2$ and $\R{\B{x}} = \EX{\B{X} \B{X}^{\dag}} = 2\mathcal{P}_s \B{I}_2$.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
assumptions: Due to the orthogonality of Alamouti codeword

nodes.name: Average sum-rate in channel gains
nodes.statement: &C_{\text{sum}} = \nonumber \\ & \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2 \biggl[ \left(1+2\bar\gamma\frac{|\h{1}|^2 |\h{2}|^2+|\h{0}|^2\left(|\h{1}|^2 + |\h{2}|^2\right)}{|\h{1}|^2 + 2|\h{2}|^2}\right) \nonumber \\ &\times \left(1+2\bar\gamma\frac{|\h{1}|^2 |\h{2}|^2+|\h{0}|^2\left(|\h{1}|^2 + |\h{2}|^2\right)}{|\h{2}|^2 + 2|\h{1}|^2}\right) \biggr] \biggr\}

nodes.name: Instantaneous SNRs
nodes.statement:
For notational simplicity, let us denote
$\snri{i}=2\bar\gamma|\h{i}|^2$ with $i=0,1,2$.

nodes.name: High-SNR sum-rate approximation
nodes.statement: \frac{3 \ln2}{2} C_{\text{sum}} &\approx \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(\frac{\snri{1}\snri{2}}{\snri{1}+2\snri{2}}\right)} }_{I_1} + \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(\frac{\snri{1}\snri{2}}{\snri{2}+2\snri{1}}\right)} }_{I_2} \nonumber \\ &+ 2 \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(1+\frac{\snri{0}\left(\snri{1}+\snri{2}\right)}{\snri{1}\snri{2}}\right)} }_{I_3}

nodes.statement_short: At high SNR the sum-rate splits into expectations $I_1$, $I_2$, $I_3$ of logarithms of SNR ratios.

nodes.name: Integral form of I_1
nodes.statement: I_1 = \sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} \mathcal{A}_v \frac{\ln z}{1+z} z^{u} \exp(-\beta_1 z) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z} dz

nodes.label: eq:I:1:1

nodes.name: Meijer's G-function
nodes.statement:
To further simplify \eqref{eq:I:1:1}, we will express $\ln z/(1+z)$
and $\exp\left(-\alpha z\right) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z}$ in terms of
the Meijer's G-function with the help of
\cite[eq.~(8.4.6.13)]{Prudnikov:90:Book} and
\cite[eq.~(6.4.23.3)]{Prudnikov:90:Book} as follows:


\begin{align} \frac{\ln z}{1 +z}
    &=
    -\pi
    G_{3,3}^{2,2}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {0,0,1/2}  \vspace{0.2cm}\\
    {0,0,1/2} \end{array}} \right.\right)
    \\ \exp\left(-\alpha z\right) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z}
    &=
    \sqrt{\pi}
    G_{1,2}^{2,0}\left({2\alpha z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {1/2}  \vspace{0.2cm}\\
    {v,-v} \end{array}} \right. \right)
\end{align}


where $G_{p,q}^{m,n}(\cdot)$ is the Meijer's G-function
\cite[eq.~(8.2.1.1)]{Prudnikov:90:Book}.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Meijer G representation of ln z/(1+z)
nodes.statement: \frac{\ln z}{1 +z} &= -\pi G_{3,3}^{2,2}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {0,0,1/2} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {0,0,1/2} \end{array}} \right.\right)
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.label: eq:ln:1

nodes.name: Meijer G representation of exp times Bessel K
nodes.statement: \exp\left(-\alpha z\right) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z} &= \sqrt{\pi} G_{1,2}^{2,0}\left({2\alpha z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {1/2} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {v,-v} \end{array}} \right. \right)
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.label: eq:exp:1

nodes.name: Meijer G-function as special case of Fox's H-function
nodes.statement: G_{p,q}^{m,n}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(a_p)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(b_q)} \end{array}} \right.\right) = H_{p,q}^{m,n}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(a_p,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(b_q,1)} \end{array}} \right.\right)
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.label: eq:Meijer:Fox:1

nodes.name: I_1 in Fox H-functions
nodes.statement: I_1 = - &\sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \pi^{3/2} \mathcal{A}_v \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} z^u \exp\left[-\left(\beta_1 - \alpha\right)z\right] \nonumber \\ &\times H_{3,3}^{2,2}\left[ {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1)} \end{array}} \right.\right] \nonumber \\ &\times H_{1,2}^{2,0}\left[{2\alpha z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(1/2,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(v,1),(-v,1)} \end{array}} \right. \right] dz
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.label: eq:I:1:2

nodes.name: Generalized Fox's H-function
nodes.statement:
Then, the integral $I_1$ can be calculated with the help of
\cite[eq.~(2.6.2)]{Mathai:78:Book} as follows:

    \\

H_{1,[3:1],0,[3:2]}^{1,2,0,2,2}\left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}

nodes.name: Exponential-decay path loss
nodes.statement:
The path loss of each link follows an
exponential-decay model: if the distance between the two sources is
equal to $d$, then $\CP{0} \propto d^{-\alpha}$ where an exponent of
$\alpha=4$ corresponds to a typical non line-of-sight propagation
\cite{HTHC:08:VTCSpring}.

nodes.name: Two-way DASTC outperforms one-way DASTC
nodes.statement:
More importantly, the proposed two-way DASTC scheme outperforms the
conventional one-way system in terms of the spectral efficiency in
the whole considered range of SNR. In particular, at SNR=30 dB, the
proposed scheme enhances the average sum-rate to 3.8 bps/Hz in both
Example 1 and 2 compared to the conventional one.

conventional one-way system in terms of the spectral efficiency in
the whole considered range of SNR

nodes.name: PDF of Z = gamma_i gamma_j/(gamma_i + 2 gamma_j)
nodes.statement: Let $\snri{i}$ and $\snri{j}$ be statistically independent and not necessarily identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) exponential random variables with hazard rate $\snravei{i}$ and $\snravei{j}$, respectively. Suppose that the ratio of $Z$ takes the form \begin{align} Z=\frac{\snri{i} \snri{j}}{\snri{i} +2\snri{j}} \end{align} Then, we obtain the PDF of random variable $Z$ as \begin{align} \PDF{Z}{z} = \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \left[\alpha\Bessel{0}{\alpha z} + \beta_i \Bessel{1}{\alpha z}\right] \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$. \begin{proof} Let us rewrite $Z$ in a more tractable form as \begin{align} Z = \left(X + Y\right)^{-1} \end{align} where $X=1/\snri{i}$ and $Y=2/\snri{j}$. Then, after some algebraic simplifications together with the help of \cite[eq.~(3.471.9)]{GR:00:Book}, the moment generating function (MGF) of $X$ and $Y$ can be expressed as, respectively \begin{align} &\MGF{X}{s} = \EXs{X}{\exp\left(-s x\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \\ &\MGF{Y}{s} = \EXs{Y}{\exp\left(-s y\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} As can be seen from \eqref{eq:Z}, since $1/Z$ is the sum of two statistically independent random variables, by using \eqref{eq:MGF:X} and \eqref{eq:MGF:Y}, the MGF of $1/Z$ can be expressed as \begin{align} \MGF{1/Z}{s} = 4\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}s \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} Then, the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $1/Z$, $\CDF{1/Z}{x}$, can be shown as \begin{eqnarray} \CDF{1/Z}{x} =1- \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{\MGF{1/Z}{s}/s\}|_{1/x} \end{eqnarray} where $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{.\}$ stands for the inverse Laplace transform. From \eqref{eq:MGF:1:Z} and \eqref{eq:CDF:1:Z} together with \cite[eq.~(13.2.20)]{RK:66:Book}, we have \begin{align} \CDF{Z}{z} = 1 - \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \Bessel{1}{\alpha z} \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$. By differentiating \eqref{eq:CDF:Z:1} with respect to $z$ and using the fact that $\tfrac{d\Bessel{v}{z}}{dz}=-\Bessel{v-1}{z}-\tfrac{v}{z}\Bessel{v}{z}$ \cite[eq.~(8.486.12)]{GR:00:Book}, we obtain \eqref{eq:PDF:Z:1} which completes the proof. \end{proof}
